editorial:
Imagine choosing a huge pile of money over the love of your life. That is exactly what Bernice does, and it sets off a chain of drama that lasts for years. You get to follow Bernice as she tries to make up for her mistakes by giving her daughter, Janet, every luxury possible. It feels like a classic soap opera where greed and love are constantly fighting. The vibe is very heavy on family tension, and you will find yourself wondering if Bernice can actually save her daughter from making the same greedy mistakes she made in her youth.

What really works here is the way the story mirrors itself across two generations. You will see some slow moments because it is an older film, but the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy old-school dramas with big lessons about money, you should definitely check this out. Since it is a silent era piece, you might want to look for a high-quality restored version. Adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the best way to see the details, but renting it on Apple TV is a great way to start if you just want a quick movie night.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Janet realizes that the wealthy Philip is not who she thought he was. She discovers that her mother actually tried to push Philip away to protect her from a life of greed. After a big confrontation with the now-rich Tom Richards, Janet sees the truth. She forgives her mother for her past choices and decides to marry her loyal friend Larry instead, finally choosing true love over money.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old Hollywood stories and family dramas.
